source.author: cic
source.text: et ego feci, qui litteras Graecas senex didici, quas quidem sic avide arripui quasi diuturnam sitim explere cupiens, ut ea ipsa mihi nota essent, quibus me nunc exemplis uti videtis.
source.text_original: et ego feci, qui litteras Graecas senex didici, quas quidem sic avide arripui quasi diuturnam sitim explere cupiens, ut ea ipsa mihi nota essent, quibus me nunc exemplis uti videtis.
source.text_english: And I too have done so, for I learned Greek letters when I was old, and I seized upon them with such eagerness, as though I were trying to quench a long-standing thirst, so that the very things I now use as examples might be familiar to me, as you see.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: nec mirum, cum etiam Cato, Romani generis disertissimus, censorius iam et senex, Graecas litteras nec erubuerit nec desperauerit discere.
reuse.text_original: nec mirum, cum etiam Cato, Romani generis disertissimus, censorius iam et senex, Graecas litteras nec erubuerit nec desperauerit discere.
reuse.text_english: Nor is it surprising, since even Cato, the most eloquent man of the Roman race, already a censor and an old man, neither blushed nor despaired to learn Greek letters.
